content.title: About
content.content: Frozen baked potato fries are pre‑cut strips that are blanched, flash‑frozen, and ready to bake in the oven. When baked they develop a crispy golden exterior while staying soft inside. The product is convenient to store in the freezer and can be prepared quickly without added oil.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Frozen french fries first appeared in the United States in the 1950s as a fast‑food convenience.
A light coating of vegetable oil and special batter mixes are often used to achieve a crunchy crust.
French fries are one of the most popular side dishes worldwide, especially in fast‑food restaurants.
Rapid‑freeze technology helps retain much of the flavor and nutrients of the potatoes.
In many countries fries are served with ketchup, mayonnaise, cheese sauce, or a variety of seasonings.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, which supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Despite heat processing, some vitamin C remains, providing antioxidant benefits.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: When made from whole potatoes, fries contain dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Energy supply
items.content: Potatoes provide a quick source of carbohydrates useful for replenishing energy after physical activity.

items.title: Low in trans fats
items.content: Baked fries prepared without hydrogenated oils do not contain trans fats.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: French fries are calorie‑dense due to carbs and sometimes added oil; portion control is recommended.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: They are often salted, which can increase sodium intake and affect blood pressure.

items.title: Acrylamide
items.content: Prolonged baking at high temperatures can form acrylamide, a potential toxin; aim for a golden, not dark, crust.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may be allergic to potatoes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bake the fries in a preheated oven at 200 °C for 12‑15 minutes until golden and crisp. Serve hot with your favorite sauces such as ketchup, mayo, cheese sauce, garlic aioli, or sprinkle with seasonings. They can also be added to salads, tacos, or used as a side for meat dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen fries in an airtight bag in the freezer at –18 °C. After thawing, cook immediately and do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
